title: Name why install.sh skipped the published binary, and retry before giving up
intent: install.sh falls back to a multi-minute cargo build without naming the transport error, while install.ps1 already interpolates its own. Give the POSIX installer the same answer and stop a blip from reaching the fallback at all.
action: Widen installer_contracts.rs::install_ps1_names_why_the_published_binary_was_skipped into both_installers_name_why_the_published_binary_was_skipped, adding the two install.sh assertions, and watch them fail. Then in scripts/install.sh: capture the transport's stderr in fetch() as FETCH_ERR, interpolate it into both fallback log lines (omitting the parenthetical when empty), and add --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --connect-timeout 10 to curl and --tries=3 --timeout=10 to wget. Finish with the regen chain so the release manifest re-hashes install.sh.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test installer_contracts --test installer_invocations --test instruction_laws && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

trace.outcome: install.sh now names the transport error on both published-binary fallback lines and retries three times with a connect deadline; the contract test asserts both installers
deviations: Added a second test and a third assertion beyond plan.md — curl's multi-line stderr split the log verdict from its reason on the first driven run, so the one-line collapse is pinned as its own contract

Added a third assertion and a second test beyond the plan: curl writes multi-line diagnostics, and the first driven run stranded the closing paren and the building-from-source verdict on their own lines — the reason had to be collapsed to one line to be readable, so the collapse is pinned too

mistakes.wrong: Wrote the tag-resolution fetch as a pipeline the way the original did, which runs fetch in a subshell where FETCH_ERR dies with it
mistakes.better: the reason would have been silently lost again, caught only while re-reading the edit — when a function must return a side effect, fetch to a temp FILE and never down a pipe

report.outcome: install.sh captures curl/wget stderr in FETCH_ERR, renders it as a one-line parenthetical on both fallback log lines, and retries 3x with a 10s connect deadline; installer_contracts.rs now asserts both installers name their reason
report.tests: cargo test --test installer_contracts --test installer_invocations --test instruction_laws && bee dev release-manifest --check — green:live — 15+2+9 passed and 340 manifest files match, with the two new assertions watched RED first; beyond that the patched installer was RUN twice against the real releases API: the happy path printed "binary v2.33.3 bee-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (checksum verified) — no build needed" and --ref v0.0.0-nope printed "binary no downloadable asset at v0.0.0-nope (curl: (28) Connection timed out after 10002 milliseconds curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404) — building from source", which is the whole point of the change on one line
